items.summary: the IRGC says three oil tankers suffered a severe explosion and fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, which changes yesterday's account of Iran's navy setting ships ablaze.
items.matters: Al Jazeera reports this as an IRGC claim that is not independently confirmed, and Qatar's prime minister told it the region cannot withstand another US-Iran escalation.

items.headline: Qatar's PM tries to revive US-Iran talks after meeting Rubio

items.matters: this is the diplomatic track that was due to run alongside the Hormuz incidents, and the US Treasury sanctioned more than two dozen Iranian entities in "shadow banking" networks on Monday.

items.headline: Commission proposes a 22nd Russia sanctions package that includes a sports ban
items.summary: Ursula von der Leyen presented it on Monday, with 60 banks removed from SWIFT, a crypto sanctions task force and a visa ban for Russians who fought in the war. It also bars Russian teams and athletes from competing under the Russian flag at EU events.
items.matters: all 27 member states must endorse it before it takes effect, and it follows the EU's largest listing against Russia, about 1,600 officials and companies tied to its arms industry.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at the European Council, Brussels, Belgium, November 20, 2026 [Nicolas Tucat/AFP] By Al Jazeera Staff and AP Published On 23 Nov 2026 23 Nov 2026 The European Commission has proposed new sanctions against Russia targeting its banks, crypto platforms, and participation in sporting events.

Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen introduced the 22nd package of sanctions on Monday, which includes a ban on Russian teams and individual athletes competing under the country’s flag at events in the European Union.

“We are striking harder at Russia’s ways to finance its war, by targeting its banks and crypto platforms,” von der Leyen wrote in a post on X, adding that the EU will be “shutting the door to its participation in European sports and cultural events”.

Von der Leyen said 60 banks will be removed from the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) messaging system used for international payments under the new proposals, which are intended to maintain economic pressure on Russia, almost five years into its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

She announced the creation of a crypto sanctions task force seeking to curb countries helping Russia to evade sanctions.

The commission also proposed a ban on visas for Russians who had fought in the war in Ukraine.

“Russian ex-combatants pose a security risk to Europe. They cannot be allowed to wander freely across our countries,” von der Leyen said.

The plan also put forward restrictions on financial flows from Russian sponsors to sports and cultural associations based in the EU. Russian nationals would also no longer be allowed to hold leadership positions on the governing bodies of sports federations.

The proposed package must be endorsed by all 27 EU member countries before going into force and comes just over a month after the bloc posted the largest listing of sanctions against Russia, targeting about 1,600 Russian officials and companies linked to its arms industry.

The EU has already slapped sanctions on more than 4,200 people and entities, including Russian President Vladimir Putin and several energy companies.

items.headline: Pennsylvania reports a ninth measles death as the US passes 5,800 cases
items.summary: the latest victim was an unvaccinated Centre County resident, and the state has 1,638 confirmed cases across 46 counties and 330 hospitalisations.
items.matters: the CDC's 5,838 confirmed cases as of 19 November are its highest count since 1991, and November alone has more than doubled the 2,289 cases reported for all of 2025.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info A sign is posted outside a Pennsylvania Department of Health measles vaccination clinic located, Peach Bottom, Pennsylvania, October 20, 2026 [Matt Rourke/AP] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 24 Nov 2026 24 Nov 2026 Pennsylvania health officials have reported another death linked to the ongoing measles outbreak, bringing the state’s death toll associated with the highly contagious viral disease to nine.

The state Department of Health confirmed on Monday the death of an unvaccinated resident of Centre County in central ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Pennsylvania who tested positive for measles.

Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, has recorded 1,638 confirmed measles cases across 46 counties so far in 2026, including 330 hospitalisations.

The nine deaths were recorded across five counties, as Lancaster County accounted ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌for three deaths, while Jefferson County reported two.

Virginia recorded its first measles-related death in more than three decades on Friday, just days after the United States lost its hard-fought designation as having eliminated the highly contagious virus.

Meanwhile, Wisconsin has reported two deaths, and New York state has recorded one child death linked to the disease.

However, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported only six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, without specifying the ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠states where the deaths were recorded.

The discrepancy between state and federal tolls emerged earlier this year after the health agency, under US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.

The US Department of Health and Human Services said it ⁠⁠⁠⁠was “saddened to hear of another death in Pennsylvania”, adding that the CDC has provided the state with nearly $4m in one-time emergency funding for ⁠⁠⁠⁠response efforts in 2027.

A total of 5,838 measles cases were confirmed across the country this year as of November 19, according to CDC data. The figure is the highest number reported by the CDC since 1991.

Children below the age of five account for 18 percent of cases, while children between the ages of five and 19 make up 41 percent of cases.

The number of confirmed cases in November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed measles cases reported for the full year of 2025.

items.headline: Rosyjski dron rozpoznawczy na kilka minut wleciał nad Polskę koło Dorohuska
items.summary: wojsko dało zgodę na zestrzelenie, ale po zawróceniu drona na wschód z niej nie skorzystało, a RCB wydało alert dla wschodnich powiatów Lubelszczyzny, odwołany tuż przed północą.
items.matters: dron, który miał kamery i napęd odrzutowy, lecąc podczas wieczornego rosyjskiego ataku na Ukrainę, był śledzony przez trzy systemy obrony powietrznej, a DORSZ uzasadnił brak strzału ryzykiem dla ludności cywilnej i skutkami zestrzelenia.
items.body:
Skomentuj Podczas wieczornego rosyjskiego nalotu na Ukrainę w polską przestrzeń powietrzną w okolicy Dorohuska na kilka minut wleciał rosyjski odrzutowy dron obserwacyjny – wynika z informacji PAP zbliżonych do MON.

fot. Akimov Igor / / Shutterstock Noc z poniedziałku na wtorek to kolejna, podczas której Rosja atakuje Ukrainę rakietami i dronami; Rządowe Centrum Bezpieczeństwa wydało alert dla powiatów we wschodniej części woj. lubelskiego ostrzegający przed zagrożeniem z powietrza i apelujący o znalezienie bezpiecznego miejsca.

O uruchomieniu systemów przeciwlotniczych i lotnictwa poinformowało w poniedziałek wieczorem Dowództwo Operacyjne Rodzajów Sił Zbrojnych. Chwilę przed północą RCB odwołało alert, informując o braku zagrożenia na terenie Polski.

Jak dowiedziała się PAP w źródłach zbliżonych do resortu obrony, podczas wieczornego ataku na Ukrainę jeden z rosyjskich dronów odrzutowych wtargnął w polską przestrzeń powietrzną w okolicy Dorohuska. Źródła zaznaczają, że dron wyposażony był w aparaturę obserwacyjną – m.in. kamery – i jego zadaniem było najprawdopodobniej prowadzenie rozpoznania.

Dron przebywał w polskiej przestrzeni – jak wskazują źródła – przez kilka minut i przez cały czas był śledzony przez polskie trzy różne systemy obrony powietrznej. Po kilku minutach lotu powrócił nad terytorium Ukrainy.

Do naruszenia polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej nawiązano także w komunikacie na X odpowiedzialnego za ochronę polskiego nieba Dowództwa Operacyjnego RSZ.

„W odpowiedzi na zagrożenie Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ uruchomiło niezbędne siły i środki systemu obrony powietrznej. Obiekt był nieprzerwanie śledzony przez wojskowe systemy radiolokacyjne na całej trasie przelotu. Sytuacja była na bieżąco monitorowana, wydano autoryzację na zestrzelenie obiektu” – wskazało w komunikacie Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ.

DORSZ dodaje, że po tym, jak rosyjski dron zmienił kurs na wschód – z powrotem w kierunku Ukrainy – „uwzględniając potencjalne zagrożenie dla ludności cywilnej i możliwe skutki zestrzelenia obiektu, podjęto decyzję o wstrzymaniu się od użycia uzbrojenia w związku z utrzymującym się ryzykiem wyrządzenia szkód”.

„Podkreślamy, że Siły Zbrojne RP nieprzerwanie monitorują sytuację w przestrzeni powietrznej, a siły i środki systemu obrony powietrznej pozostają w stałej gotowości do reagowania na wszelkie zagrożenia. Zapewnienie bezpieczeństwa polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej pozostaje naszym niezmiennym priorytetem” – zapewnia Dowództwo.

items.headline: NATO przyznaje Polsce jeden samolot AWACS po posiedzeniu Rady Północnoatlantyckiej
items.summary: wiceminister Paweł Zalewski mówi, że część polskich propozycji wzmocnienia obrony powietrznej spotkała się z bardzo pozytywnym odzewem.
items.matters: kolejne propozycje trafią na przyszłotygodniowe spotkanie szefów dyplomacji NATO, a Zalewski przyznaje, że sojusznicze zasady użycia broni wciąż odpowiadają czasom pokoju, więc ich zmiana jest dopiero rozważana.
items.body:
Skomentuj Część polskich propozycji w sprawie wzmocnienia obrony spotkała się z pozytywną odpowiedzią; do dyspozycji Polski będzie postawiony jeden samolot wczesnego ostrzegania AWACS - oznajmił w poniedziałek wiceszef MON Paweł Zalewski po spotkaniu Rady Północnoatlantyckiej w Brukseli.

/ NATO W poniedziałek w Kwaterze Głównej NATO w Brukseli doszło do spotkania Rady Północnoatlantyckiej - najważniejszego organu decyzyjnego Sojuszu. Rozmowy odbyły się w związku z piątkowym rosyjskim atakiem na zachodnią Ukrainę, podczas którego w przestrzeń powietrzną w południowo-wschodniej Polsce wtargnęły trzy rosyjskie pociski manewrujące Ch-101.

Wiceminister przekazał, że wśród sojuszników nie było nikogo, kto by wątpił w intencjonalność działań Rosji.

Zalewski powiedział na briefingu prasowym, że podczas spotkania przekazał analizę polityczną dotyczącą piątkowych wydarzeń oraz płynące z nich wnioski, a szef Służby Kontrwywiadu Wojskowego gen. bryg. Jarosław Stróżyk mówił o ataku z perspektywy wojskowej. Dodał, że wraz z pozostałymi uczestnikami spotkania rozważali polskie propozycje, sprowadzające się do zwiększenia zdolności obronnych, w tym dotyczących obrony powietrznej NATO.

- Część z (propozycji) spotkała się z bardzo pozytywną odpowiedzią. (...) Potwierdzona została decyzja, że (...) do dyspozycji Polski będzie postawiony jeden samolot wczesnego ostrzegania AWACS - poinformował wiceszef MON. Wcześniej Zalewski mówił, że Polska w Brukseli będzie występowała o wzmocnienie obrony samolotami, które są w dyspozycji państw NATO.

Zalewski zapowiedział także, że w przyszłym tygodniu odbędzie się spotkanie ministrów spraw zagranicznych państw NATO, podczas którego zostaną rozważane kolejne propozycje Polski ws. wzmocnienia obrony.

Wiceszef MON relacjonował, że wszyscy ambasadorowie krajów NATO, obecni podczas spotkania, „wyrażali pełną solidarność z Polską w obliczu prowokacji rosyjskich”. - (Ambasadorowie) mieli świadomość, że atak piątkowy nie był odizolowany, że to jest część większej całości, że to jest część tej eskalacji rosyjskiej wobec NATO - oznajmił.

Zalewski powiadomił, że przekazał informację o potrzebach polskich sił zbrojnych, służących wzmocnieniu zdolności obrony powietrznej. - Jestem bardzo zbudowany jednością Sojuszu. Wszyscy ambasadorowie, którzy zabierali głos, a zabierali głos wszyscy ambasadorowie państw członkowskich NATO, wyrażali solidarność, pełną solidarność z nami w obliczu tych prowokacji rosyjskich - podkreślił.

Według niego uczestnicy spotkania mieli świadomość, że piątkowy atak nie był odizolowany i jest częścią większej…

items.headline: Rząd przyjął projekt ustawy, który kończy coroczne wnioski o 800 plus
items.summary: ZUS ma automatycznie przedłużać świadczenie na podstawie poprzedniego wniosku, jeśli sytuacja rodziny się nie zmieniła.
items.matters: nowe zasady mają działać od 1 czerwca 2027 roku, ale projekt musi jeszcze przejść przez Sejm i dostać podpis prezydenta, a od 2027 roku o świadczenie będą mogli się starać także dziadkowie i inni krewni, którym sąd powierzył codzienną opiekę nad dzieckiem.
items.body:
Sejm rozpoczął prace nad projektem, który ma znacząco ułatwić życie rodzicom pobierającym świadczenie 800 plus. Od 2027 roku ma nastąpić koniec corocznego składania wniosków. ZUS ma automatycznie przedłużać prawo do świadczenia, jeśli dane beneficjenta nie uległy zmianie. Nowe przepisy, przygotowane przez Ministerstwo Rodziny, Pracy i Polityki Społecznej, zostały pozytywnie zaopiniowane przez rząd i trafiły do parlamentu.

Zdjęcie ilustracyjne / Shutterstock Najważniejsza zmiana dotyczy zasad przyznawania świadczenia. Do tej pory co roku rodzice musieli pilnować terminów, by nie stracić pieniędzy na dzieci – wystarczyła chwila nieuwagi, spóźnienie z wnioskiem i można było pożegnać się z częścią świadczenia. Od 1 czerwca 2027 roku (na nowy okres świadczeniowy) ten obowiązek w większości przypadków ma zniknąć – projekt ustawy zakłada, że ZUS sam odnowi prawo do 800 plus, bazując na danych z poprzedniego wniosku.

Automatyczne przedłużenie przywilejów ma na celu eliminację formalności, które do tej pory zaprzątały głowy milionom rodzin. Nowy system pozwoli uniknąć nerwów, zagubionych wniosków i niepotrzebnego stresu. Jeśli sytuacja rodzinna nie zmieni się i dane zgłoszone do ZUS będą aktualne, rodzice nie muszą nic robić, by kontynuować pobieranie 800 plus.

Nowe zasady nie mają obejmować wszystkich. Zgodnie z projektem, wniosek o 800 plus wciąż będzie musiał złożyć rodzic lub opiekun w takich przypadkach, jak:

- narodziny dziecka w trakcie roku, - powrót z dzieckiem z zagranicy, - rozpoczęcie sprawowania opieki, gdy opiekun przejmuje dziecko po raz pierwszy.

Wciąż aktualizować dane będą musieli ci, których sytuacja rodzinna ulegnie zmianie – ZUS na tej podstawie zadecyduje o dalszym wypłacaniu świadczenia.

Projekt nowelizacji przewiduje także rozszerzenie grona uprawnionych. Od 2027 roku prawo do 800 plus mają zyskać także np. babcie, dziadkowie i inni krewni, którym sąd powierzył tzw. bieżącą pieczę nad dzieckiem, choć nie zostali formalnie opiekunem prawnym czy rodziną zastępczą. Dzięki zmianom osoby faktycznie wychowujące dzieci, a pomijane do tej pory, będą mogły otrzymać wsparcie finansowe.

Pełne wdrożenie automatycznych przelewów jest planowane na czerwiec 2027 roku. W tym czasie ZUS ma przygotować specjalne systemy informatyczne, które przejmą część obowiązków od rodziców i opiekunów.

Projekt wciąż jest na etapie prac sejmowych. Musi jeszcze przejść głosowania, otrzymać podpis prezydenta i zostać ogłoszony w Dzienniku Ustaw.

items.headline: Pakiet CPN obowiązuje tylko do końca roku, a decyzja o przedłużeniu wciąż nie zapadła
items.summary: w porannej rozmowie RMF FM minister energii Miłosz Motyka ma odpowiadać, czy rząd przedłuży program na obecnych zasadach i czy objąć go LPG.

items.body:
Tylko do końca roku obowiązuje pakiet CPN. Na podjęcie decyzji zostało niewiele czasu. Co zrobi rząd? Czy program zostanie przedłużony na dotychczasowych zasadach? Czy jest szansa, że gaz LPG zostanie nim objęty? Gościem w Porannej rozmowie w RMF FM będzie Miłosz Motyka, minister energii.

Gościem Porannej rozmowy w RMF FM (fot. Marcin Suchmiel) / RMF FM Projekt ustawy o ochronie części odbiorców gazu w 2027 r. trafił do prac w Sejmie. Jeśli ostatecznie zostanie zaakceptowany przez parlament, co to będzie oznaczało dla osób ogrzewających domy gazem? Czy ustawa zyska przychylność prezydenta?

Zapytamy także o ceny prądu. Czy rząd pracuje nad rozwiązaniami, które pozwolą je zamrozić w 2027 roku? Co z cenami pelletu? Czy w tym przypadku rząd też myśli o jakimś wsparciu osób ogrzewających domy pelletem?

Na rozmowę Tomasza Terlikowskiego zapraszamy tuż po godz. 8:00 do RMF FM, internetowego Radia RMF24, na stronę RMF24.pl, aplikacji RMF ON i naszych mediów społecznościowych!

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds after Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia rose 31.48% on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 4.73% to 7,237.23, the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% and the Dow 3.01%, while the VIX fell more than 25%.
items.matters: the board reversed under pressure from shareholders, employees and Trump, and Bankier calls it a technical rebound from an oversold market, with the Nasdaq still about 13% below its October peak and thin trading this week with no session on Thursday.
items.body:
Skomentuj Bezwarunkowo i w trybie natychmiastowym Jensen Huang powrócił na stanowisko prezydenta i CEO Nvidii. Ta informacja dźwignęła kurs technologicznego giganta o niewiarygodne 31%, co na mocno wyprzedanym rynku doprowadziło do potężnych zwyżek.

fot. Kylie Cooper / Reuters / / / FORUM Nasdaq Composite zyskał 6,51% po tym, jak w piątek zanurkował o 5,3% i znalazł się najniżej od kwietnia. Po poniedziałkowej sesji Nasdaq nawiązką odrobił piątkowe straty, ale wciąż znajduje się 13% poniżej październikowego szczytu hossy.

Tak wielki entuzjazm inwestorów wywołany został informacją z Nvidii, której rada dyrektorów uległa presji akcjonariuszy, pracowników i samego prezydenta Donalda Trumpa przywracając na wcześniejsze stanowiska prezesa i założyciela spółki Jensena Huanga. To zdjęło ze stołu część obaw o przyszłość Nvidii i wyniosło kurs akcje producenta chipów o 31,48% w górę. Jest to coś, co w przypadku tak wielkiej spółki praktycznie się nie zdarza. Warto jednak pamiętać, że przez poprzedni miesiąc kurs Nvidii spadł o 44%. Ma zatem co odrabiać.

- Było zdecydowanie wielu ludzi, którzy chcieli jego powrotu. Nie jest możliwym ocenić, czy w jakim stopniu zdecydowała presja akcjonariuszy, w jakim pracowników, a w jakim rządu – skwitował Steve Sosnick, główny strateg Interactive Brokers cytowany przez agencję Reuters. Wolta rady dyrektorów Nvidii jest o tyle niespodziewana, że jeszcze w ubiegłym tygodniu kategorycznie wykluczała powrót Jensena Huanga. Jak widać wiarygodność nie jest jej mocną stroną.

Optymizm udzielił się całemu sektorowi technologicznemu na Wall Street. Notowania Tesli wzrosły o 11,5%. Kurs akcji Micron Technology poszedł w górę o 19%, Intela o 16%, a walory Mety i Alphabetu zyskiwały po przeszło 6%.

Warto przy tym mieć świadomość, że dzisiejsza zwyżka nie przesądza o tym, że wszystkie obawy dotyczące przyszłości boomu na AI odeszły w zapomnienie. Inwestorzy nadal próbują wycenić, kiedy, kto i ile zarobi na obsłudze generatywnej sztucznej inteligencji. Po prostu dobra dla inwestorów wiadomość od Nvidii padła na grunt mocno wyprzedanego i przecenionego rynku. Tylko w zeszłym tygodniu główne nowojorskie indeksy giełdowe zanotowały najsilniejsze spadki od covidowego krachu z marca 2020 roku.

items.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.summary: the board voted unanimously to bring him back as president, CEO and director, less than a week after saying his return was not under consideration, and the White House says President Trump dialled into a board meeting hours before the vote.
items.matters: Nvidia says input came from senior US government levels and that the return poses no national security risk, and chair Harvey Jones stays in post after Huang's 12 November removal.
items.body:
There's no telling what caused the Nvidia board to vote unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO less than a week after saying his return wasn’t under consideration – except reportedly the threat of having one's head ripped off and brain peed on – but that really doesn't matter, at least as far as shareholders need to be concerned: Jensen's back in charge and all’s right in the world of chip stocks.

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said of the decision to reinstate him, calling it an honor.

Nvidia kicked its former-cum-current CEO and president to the curb on November 12, but not over allegations that he may have been sleeping with a suspected Chinese spy – it was affairs at Nvidia with his subordinates that appears to have been the last straw with Nvidia directors.

Nvidia stock has tumbled since Huang’s ouster, and much of the rest of the tech stock world followed suit. Nvidia insiders and tech heavyweights have been pushing for Huang’s return for about as long as he was unemployed, but calls for his return from the US federal government may have been the catalyst for a change of heart among Nvidia leadership who didn’t want Huang back.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," Nvidia said in its statement announcing Huang’s return.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones added. Jones was made Nvidia's first board chair upon Huang’s resignation, and will remain in that role.

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. "The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

items.headline: Anthropic researcher claims Claude helped prove the Riemann Hypothesis
items.summary: Levent Alpöge posted a four-page note, backed by roughly 240 MB of Lean code and about 250,000 pages of generated text that he calls "slop".
items.matters: Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative say they have "full confidence", but Kevin Buzzard says "we don't even know why the theorem is true", and the Clay Institute has only moved the problem from "unsolved" to "active".
items.body:
If the AI can't explain what it's proven, are we actually any closer to understanding?

But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box?

That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure.

In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them.

The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2.

Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here. What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution.

Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros. There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that.

Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate.

The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs.

The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from…

items.headline: Critical Cisco Expressway RCE is being exploited
items.summary: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) gives attackers root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, and CISA added it to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 20 November.
items.matters: Cisco disclosed the bug in October and has a fix, and federal agencies were told to patch by Monday.
items.body:
Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers.

CVE-2026-76466, which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services.

At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability.

That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available.

Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information.

The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6.

The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices.

A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday.

items.headline: Microsoft's final report on the 12–14 November Microsoft 365 outage blames a July Windows gateway defect
items.summary: a code change combined with a failover and reduced capacity took down Exchange Online, with more than 80% of North American gateway servers unresponsive at the worst point.
items.matters: Microsoft says queued enterprise mail was eventually delivered, but consumer messages to mailboxes inactive for over 30 days expired. The fixes include a 48-hour retry window, failure isolation and testing on newer hardware.
items.body:
Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures.

The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer.

A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments.

The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14.

Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost.

The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive.

The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix.

Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising.

Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom.

Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing.

items.headline: Amazon buys Decart AI's optimisation stack to keep Trainium busy
items.summary: it is an asset purchase covering the Decart Optimization Stack, its technology and the three founders' engineering team, and it works across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and AWS Trainium.
items.matters: Bloomberg's sources value it at about $7.5bn, which neither company has confirmed. Decart's Lucy and Oasis models are excluded.
items.body:
Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations.

The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold.

DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips.

Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs.

An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back.

Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion.

items.body:
Unite Seoul 2026 kicked off a new chapter for Unity. The livestreamed keynote was packed with announcements spanning the Unity Engine, monetization, and collaboration tooling that all build toward the next generation of Unity — Unity 7.

You can watch the full presentation, or read on for an overview of the event’s biggest announcements.

This post describes features, capabilities, and timing still in development. These reflect our current plans, but actual results and availability could differ materially and are subject to change without notice.

Unity CEO and President Matthew Bromberg opened the keynote by pointing to a reel of games built entirely in Korea, framing them as proof of what he called the country’s “Ppalli Ppalli spirit” — not just speed, but a refusal to let studios with a mobile-first ambition experience creative compromise. He was candid about the moment the industry is in, acknowledging “real pain and more than a little anxiety about the future” amid rapid change.

He then got to the news: developers expecting to hear about continued iterations in the Unity 6 generation got something bigger instead. “A new point release wouldn’t be enough for this moment,” Bromberg said. “Instead of new point release, I’m here today to share something else. And that thing is Unity 7!

He described Unity 7 as a platform rebuilt for a world where “diverse teams of creators and coding agents” work side by side across every part of development — faster (thanks to a CoreCLR-modernized core, near-instant Play Mode, and dynamic reloads that only reload what changed), and more open (with a free MCP, CLI, and API built in). It also extends into monetization and growth, with built-in direct-to-consumer commerce, no-code webshops, and Unity Vector’s AI-driven player matching.

Joe Valenzuela from Unity’s engineering team kicked things off with what may be the most consequential technical announcement of the keynote: Unity will be shipping CoreCLR, arriving in Unity 7 next year. This brings full access to the modern.NET ecosystem — CoreCLR,.NET 10, and C# 14 — giving developers more expressive, higher-performance code, first-class integration with modern IDEs and official.NET debuggers, and support for MSBuild. That MSBuild support is also a step toward compiling code outside the Editor entirely, which unlocks faster agentic workflows.

The bigger structural change is a new code reload model. Instead of reloading an entire domain on every change, Unity will reload only what’s necessary, cumulatively saving significant time over a project’s life.

items.headline: NuGet.org adds staged publishing
items.summary: packages upload privately, go through malware, signature and repository-signing checks, and stay hidden until a maintainer promotes them on the website.
items.matters: it is opt-in, basic CLI support (`dotnet package stage push`) needs the .NET 11 RC2 SDK, promotion needs 2FA, and group promotion is not atomic, so it is worth a look if you publish plugin dependencies.
items.body:
A successful build tells you that your pipeline finished. It does not tell you that you meant to release. Today, we are introducing staged publishing on NuGet.org, available to all package publishers, so you can prepare and validate packages privately before making an explicit decision to publish them.

Upload a security fix ahead of its coordinated disclosure. Gather the packages for a feature release without exposing an unfinished set. Let automation prepare a large update, then review it on NuGet.org before it reaches the people who depend on it.

With a normal package push, upload starts the public publishing process. Staged publishing adds a place to stop: the package goes through NuGet.org validation, but stays private until an authorized maintainer promotes it through the website.

That gives you time to review what you are about to ship, fix validation problems, and choose the release moment.

Staging is opt-in. Existing dotnet nuget push workflows continue to work. You can adopt staging for a security-sensitive package or a coordinated release without changing every publishing workflow at once.

Staging also differs from unlisting. An unlisted package can still be restored by its exact version. A staged package is not available to consumers at all.

The website is where you review staged content and approve its release. You can stage a single package or organize related packages into a staging group.

On the NuGet.org upload page, choose the staging option under Publishing Mode when uploading your package. You can also upload from your pipeline using the CLI example below.

NuGet.org runs the package through its validation pipeline, including malware scanning, signature checks, and repository signing. Once validation succeeds, the package is ready for promotion. It stays out of public package pages, search results, and restore operations.

You can inspect the staged package and its validation status in the website’s package management experience. If validation fails, fix the problem and stage a replacement before release day.

Staging does not provide a private restore feed, even for the owner. Test your packages and their dependencies using a local or private feed first, then stage the release artifacts on NuGet.org.

A staging group collects the packages for a release under one staging owner, either a user or an organization. For example, a library, its integrations, and its analyzers can share a group for an upcoming feature release.

items.matters: the North West Ambulance Service says over 50 people were treated for eye and breathing symptoms, with no serious injuries reported.
items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google Concertgoers were evacuated from Don Toliver’s show at Co-op Live tonight after an unknown substance believed to be tear gas was released in the crowd. Social media videos from the Manchester venue show fans coughing and covering their faces during “TORE UP,” midway through the planned set. Toliver left the stage during “K9” and did not return. “Due to unforeseen circumstances, the show is now finished,” a Co-op Live representative said after the lights came on. Greater Manchester Police arrived on the scene with emergency crews including the Hazardous Area Response Team as over 12,000 people were evacuated.

"Anyone at last night's event who has since noticed side-effects or become ill should attend their local hospital," GMP say in a statement. "Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident."

In May 2017, 22 people were killed in a terrorist attack at nearby AO Arena (then Manchester Arena) following an Ariana Grande concert. items.matters: Styles, Cher and Kraftwerk all play Glastonbury for the first time, and tickets sold out before the line-up was revealed.
items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google There was no Glastonbury Festival in 2026. Every few years, the massive English music festival takes a year off so that the soil at Worthy Farm, the festival site, can recover. Today, however, the Glastonbury bookers have announced the initial lineup for the 2027 festival. This time around, the three big Pyramid Stage headliners are Sam Fender, Harry Styles, and Billie Eilish, while Cher will play in the Sunday afternoon "legends" slot.

As The Guardian notes, this is the youngest set of Glastonbury headliners of the 21st century. Fender and Styles are both 32, and Eilish is 24. Both Eilish and Fender have played Glastonbury before — the two of them went back-to-back to close out the Pyramid Stage in 2022 — but Styles and Cher will make their Glastonbury debuts. Kraftwerk, another legendary act, will also play Glasto for the first time, as will younger acts like Angine de Poitrine, Sombr, Adéla, the Womack Sisters, and Sienna Spiro.

Even without the full festival lineup being announced yet, the bill is already predictably huge. The other acts booked to play include (deep breath) Massive Attack, Crowded House, Primal Scream, Saint Etienne, the xx, FKA twigs, Kacey Musgraves, Robyn, Lily Allen, the War On Drugs, King Gizzard And The Lizard Wizard, the Streets, Underworld, Texas, Ellie Goulding, Little Simz, Lola Young, FLO, Christine And The Queens, Young Fathers, the Avalanches, Basement Jaxx, Nia Archives, Hot Chip, De La Soul, Mike D 5D, Chvrches, Blood Orange, Thundercat, Dinosaur Jr., Westside Cowboy, Underscores, Chase & Status, Confidence Man, Ezra Collective, Leon Bridges, Tinariwen, Lianna La Havas, Florence Road, Getdown Services, Thee Sacred Souls, Atarashi Gakko!, Nao, and Ecca Vandal.

items.matters: staff fell from roughly 5,500 to 4,700, and WMG sold catalogue rights to its 50/50 Bain Capital joint venture for $233m.

The firm’s most-watched metric – recorded music subscription streaming revenues – was up 12.4% YoY at constant currency to $3.017 billion in the year-long period.

Warner also told investors that money from its AI licensing deals is on its way.

That’s fiscal Q1, or calendar Q4 (i.e., the quarter in which you’re reading these words).

Warner struck a licensing deal with Suno in November 2025. We’ll soon start to see what that deal – and Warner’s other AI partnerships – is actually worth.

In addition to publishing its Q4 and full-year results, Warner filed its annual report (10-K) with the SEC on the same day – a treasure trove of information for snoops like MBW.

By MBW’s estimate, YouTube paid Warner Music Group more than USD $1 billion in WMG’s latest fiscal year – the first time the platform’s annual contribution to WMG has crossed that threshold.

Each year, Warner’s 10-K names any customer that individually accounts for 10% or more of the company’s total revenues, and discloses the share each one supplies.

Warner’s total revenues in fiscal 2026 were $7.437 billion. And 14% of that figure (i.e., YouTube’s contribution) is approximately $1.04 billion.

A year earlier, YouTube accounted for 12% of Warner’s $6.707 billion in revenues – approximately $805 million.

On MBW’s estimates, YouTube’s contribution to Warner grew by around 29% YoY in fiscal 2026.

That’s faster in percentage terms than Spotify, whose contribution to Warner grew by around 16% YoY in fiscal 2026 to approximately $1.56 billion (21% of total revenues), and Apple, whose contribution was broadly flat at approximately $744 million (10%).

By the same estimates, YouTube now generates around $300 million more a year for Warner than Apple does; Spotify is contributing around double its Cupertino rival.

It’s also worth noting that Warner’s revenue sources have become increasingly concentrated in recent years.

In fiscal 2026, Spotify, YouTube, and Apple jointly accounted for approximately 45% of WMG’s total revenue.

That’s the highest combined share Warner has disclosed for the three platforms since YouTube first passed the 10% threshold in fiscal 2021. The figure was 42% in fiscal 2021, 40% in fiscal 2022, 41% in both fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024, and 43% in fiscal 2025.

items.headline: Eminem co-publisher Eight Mile Style adds 108 allegedly infringing AI tracks to its $47.7m Suno lawsuit
items.summary: The amended complaint, filed 19 November, brings 26 of the 269 compositions in the case into play, and the damages sought are unchanged.
items.matters: the plaintiffs call Suno's claim that it blocks artist-specific prompts "false", and UMG and Sony are still suing Suno after Warner settled in November 2025.
items.body:
Eminem co-publisher Eight Mile Style has amended its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, adding 108 more AI-generated tracks that it says infringe its songs.

The amended complaint was filed on Thursday (November 19) in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, 13 days after the original suit.

The new examples cover 26 of the 269 compositions in the case, including Lose Yourself, Stan, Mockingbird, and Without Me.

The damages Eight Mile Style is seeking are unchanged, at just over USD $47.7 million across its three claims.

The amended complaint responds to what Suno told reporters after the original suit was filed on November 6.

In its statement on the original suit, a Suno spokesperson said: “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work.

The motion the complaint refers to, filed on November 3, is Suno’s bid to have a Boston federal court dismiss a proposed class action from Jason Isbell and three other musicians.

The publisher says it believes these examples are “just the tip of the iceberg,” and that Suno has made infringing outputs for every song in the case.

The amended complaint also opens with a new introduction built around Eminem’s commercial track record.

Despite that language, the amended complaint does not add a claim over Eminem’s voice or likeness.

The plaintiffs remain Eight Mile Style and Martin Affiliated, and Eminem himself is not a party to the case.

Eight Mile Style’s three claims are also unchanged: copyright infringement, bypassing the access controls of streaming and lyrics platforms, and stripping songwriter and publisher credits from its songs.

By contrast, Elvis Presley Enterprises, which says it solely owns Presley’s likeness rights, is suing Suno under Tennessee’s ELVIS Act, a state law covering a person’s voice and likeness.

The new Eight Mile Style passages on likeness and on Suno’s press statement match, almost word for word, language in the amended complaint that the Presley plaintiffs filed on November 13.

Both cases were filed by Richard S. Busch of Adams & Reese, whose team has also filed suits against Suno this year on behalf of Round Hill Music, Gerencia 360, and Reservoir.

The bulk of the money Eight Mile Style is seeking, USD $40.35 million, is for copyright infringement.

That figure applies the legal maximum of USD $150,000 per song, available where infringement is found to be willful, to all 269 compositions.

items.summary: Fincher says the Tarantino-scripted sequel cost about $120–123m rather than the reported $200m, and Brad Pitt missed Monday's London premiere with flu.
items.matters: it reaches Netflix on 23 December, and early reviews are mixed, with TheWrap's headline calling it "an OK movie".
items.body:
The director says the Brad Pitt movie came in at around $120 million, well below the figure Quentin Tarantino gave last year.

David Fincher attends Netflix’s “The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth” New York Screening at The Plaza Hotel on November 21, 2026 in New York City.

David Fincher has pushed back on reports that The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth cost $200 million, saying the Netflix movie came in at around $120 million. In a new 90-minute interview, the director also revealed how he came to direct Quentin Tarantino’s script and how close to release the movie was finished.

The $200 million figure has followed the movie since August 2025, when Quentin Tarantino said on The Church of Tarantino podcast that it was the largest budget he’d ever been associated with and that the movie would be “in the region of $200 million.” It has been widely repeated since and would make the movie the most expensive of both Tarantino’s and Fincher’s careers.

Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he also explained why Mindhunter season 3 never happened, Fincher gave a very different number.

He says the new movie came in at around $120 to $123 million, with the increase down to it being more expensive to shoot in Los Angeles six years later. According to Fincher, the two productions had roughly the same number of shooting days and the same size of crew.

Fincher didn’t say what his figure covers. Reports earlier this year put Brad Pitt’s fee at $40 million, Fincher’s at $20 million, and Tarantino’s at more than $20 million for the script. If Fincher is quoting the cost of the shoot alone, those deals would account for most of the $80 million difference.

Fincher says Brad Pitt had been talking about another Cliff Booth project for nine or ten months before calling to ask him to read the script. Fincher was interested, as Cliff was his favorite character in the first movie, but he refused to open it until Tarantino had signed off.

Once he had permission, he read a script of around 230 pages, which he has previously said could have been a series. He called the opening scene “one of the best things I had read in many, many years” and also singled out a balcony scene.

Fincher spent a good chunk of the interview on Karen Crosby, the character played by Elizabeth Debicki. He describes her as a “giant Aussie” who takes no nonsense and acts as a gatekeeper for her most important client.

items.headline: Netflix orders an adult animated Grendel series from Matt Wagner's Dark Horse comic
items.summary: Bobak Esfarjani, an Emmy winner known for WandaVision, will showrun, and Bobbypills, the studio behind Creature Commandos, will animate.
items.matters: no cast or release date has been announced for the series, which follows Hunter Rose, a masked New York assassin.
items.body:
Netflix has ordered an adult animated adaptation of Matt Wagner’s iconic Dark Horse comic book series 'Grendel', with Emmy-winning producer Bobak Esfarjani as showrunner.

Netflix has officially green-lit an adult animated adaptation of Matt Wagner’s legendary, genre-hopping Dark Horse comic book series Grendel. The streamer has assembled an acclaimed team for the adaptation, including Emmy-winning WandaVision producer Bobak Esfarjani as showrunner.

Netflix has adapted a lot of beloved comic books over the years, from major successes like The Umbrella Academy to wildly ambitious series like The Sandman. Looking ahead to the future, the streamer isn’t slowing down anytime soon. Earlier this year, Netflix green-lit a live-action series based on the hyper-violent fantasy Barbaric by Michael Moreci. Today, Netflix has announced its next comic book adaptation, adapting the ambitious, genre-shifting Grendel, created, written, and illustrated by Matt Wagner. Incidentally, Wagner also co-created the comic book Dead Boy Detectives, which was adapted into a Netflix series of the same name in 2024.

To bring a comic as sprawling as Grendel to the small screen demands a top-tier creative team, and that’s exactly what’s been assembled. Emmy-award winning producer, Bobak Esfarjani (Widow’s Bay, WandaVision, Alien: Earth), will showrun, write and executive produce. In addition, Chris Tongue, Tim Wiesch and Jay Komas are executive producing for Dark Horse Entertainment, alongside Lydia Antonini (Locke and Key, Halo: Forward Unto Dawn), and Matt Wagner. The studio behind the animation is Bobbypills, which is best known for DC’s Creature Commandos.

No casting has been announced yet. This show has just been green-lit so further details can be expected at a later date.

Debuting in 1982 from Comico before moving to Dark Horse Comics, Grendel is a dark, neo-noir crime saga, although it’s so sprawling that tying it down to a single genre is impossible. As the series progressed, Wagner evolved it into a multi-generational sci-fi epic with as big a scale as any comic you’ll pick up. It begins with Hunter Rose, a masked New York assassin and crime lord who stops at nothing to avenge the murder of the woman he loves.

After the woman he loves is shockingly murdered, Hunter Rose devotes himself to one thing: vengeance. The wait for 'Ginny & Georgia' season 4 is shorter than expected as Netflix locks in a January 2027 release date for the hit drama.

The wait is almost over! Netflix has finally locked in the release date for Ginny & Georgia season 4, confirming the Millers will return on Thursday, January 21st, 2027. Alongside the date, we’ve also got our first proper look at the new season with a big batch of stills.

Today’s announcement finally puts a pin in what has been a long wait. Back in August, Netflix quietly moved season 4 into its 2027 slate, which ruled out the hopes of many fans that the show would be back before the end of this year. We now know that the show is set to be one of Netflix’s first big releases of the new year.

That puts the gap between seasons 3 and 4 at just over 19 months. Season 3 dropped back on June 5th, 2025, which was itself nearly two and a half years after season 2 debuted in January 2023. So while it might not feel like it, this is actually the quickest turnaround between seasons the show has had yet.

Alongside the date, Netflix has handed out a fresh synopsis for the new season, and it’s safe to say that Georgia’s legal troubles being behind her doesn’t mean smooth sailing:

When Season 4 begins, Georgia Miller has dodged a murder charge! So life is finally back to normal. Except that the Millers are broke again. And Georgia’s pregnant and doesn’t know who the father is. And strange things keep happening, hinting that maybe Georgia’s past isn’t willing to stay buried. Ginny is desperate to break the cycle of chaos, and Georgia is desperate to prove to her kids that she can. And as for Austin…well… This season it’s him against the world. The family is at a turning point. But when push comes to shove, will the Millers be able to start fresh? Or will the past pull them back in?

So, the big takeaways: Georgia walks free following the events of the season 3 finale, the Millers are back to counting pennies, and the question of who fathered Georgia’s baby is going to be front and center. “Georgia’s past isn’t willing to stay buried” also lines up nicely with the show’s season 4 theme of “Cycles and Origins,” and, of course, the arrival of Sunny Mabrey as Daisy, Georgia’s estranged mother.

items.headline: Netflix picks up Starz's Vida, with all three seasons arriving 15 December
items.summary: Tanya Saracho's drama about two estranged Mexican-American sisters in Boyle Heights has 22 episodes, with Melissa Barrera and Mishel Prada.
items.matters: each season holds a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score, and the show had been mostly unavailable on Netflix in the US and Europe.
items.body:
All three seasons of Tanya Saracho’s hit drama are heading to Netflix in most regions on December 15th.

The Starz to Netflix pipeline keeps on flowing, and this time it’s not just the US getting in on the action. We can confirm that Vida, the hit Starz drama led by Melissa Barrera and Mishel Prada, is set to arrive on Netflix on December 15th, 2026, in most regions, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, and France, among many others others.

That wide rollout makes it something of an outlier. Most of the Starz library titles Netflix has snapped up lately, such as Run the World, Blindspotting, and Dangerous Liaisons, have been US-only affairs.

Tanya Saracho created the series, taking inspiration from Richard Villegas Jr.’s short story “Pour Vida.” It follows Emma and Lyn, two estranged Mexican-American sisters who couldn’t be more different. Their mother’s death pulls the pair back to the Boyle Heights neighborhood of Los Angeles where they grew up. Once there, they inherit the family bar, a pile of debt, and a few secrets about who their mother really was.

Starz aired 22 episodes over three seasons, starting on May 6th, 2018, and wrapping up on May 31st, 2020. All three seasons are expected to drop at once on December 15th. While the show was definitely intended to go beyond three seasons, Starz ultimately made the decision to call season 3 the final season and it does end on a satisfactory note if you’re worried about it ending on a major cliffhanger.

The show was a critical darling throughout its run. Every one of its seasons sits at a perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it took home a GLAAD Media Award for Outstanding Comedy Series in 2019. Time also ranked it fourth on its list of the best TV shows of 2019. This isn’t strictly the show’s Netflix debut. Back in April 2024, select Latin American countries such as Brazil and Mexico received all three seasons.

Vida is the latest in a long line of Lionsgate and Starz titles to find a second home on Netflix. In the past year or so, we’ve seen:

items.headline: Netflix sets a Pamela Smart true crime documentary for 16 December
items.summary: The film is directed by Lyttanya Shannon and is titled "Most Hated Woman" in What's on Netflix's URL.
items.matters: it joins a busy December slate of Netflix true crime and K-drama arrivals.
items.body:
Netflix is bringing the chilling true story of the "most hated woman in America" to screens in 2026 with a brand new true-crime documentary.

There have been numerous documentaries on the subject of Pamela Smart, whose role in the murder of her husband created a media circus in 1991 and had the nation transfixed. Netflix is throwing its hat into the documentary ring, and a brand new documentary on “the most hated woman in America” is coming to the streaming service on December 16, 2026.

Netflix has confirmed that the documentary will premiere on the service on December 16, 2026.

In 1991, Gregg Smart was shot dead in the New Hampshire home he shared with his wife, Pamela. Within months, Pamela and her teenage lover, Billy Flynn, stood accused of his murder. Dubbed the most hated woman in America, Pamela became the face of a trial that held the country transfixed.

Pamela Smart is an American woman serving life without parole for her role in the May 1990 murder of her husband, Gregg Smart, in Derry, New Hampshire. Then a 22-year-old high school media coordinator, Smart was convicted in 1991 of being an accomplice to first-degree murder, conspiracy to murder, and witness tampering after prosecutors argued she manipulated her 15-year-old lover, William “Billy” Flynn, and his friends into killing him. Broadcast live on television, the trial became a media sensation that continues to draw scrutiny.

Smart maintained her innocence for many years and argued that her life sentence without parole is overly harsh, a stance she reiterated during an October 2010 appearance on The Oprah Winfrey Show. It wasn’t until June 2024 that she finally accepted her responsibility for her husband’s murder. This year, she and her legal team continue to seek an overturn of her conviction, for which she has now served 36 years.

The story of Pamela Smart has been examined in over a dozen documentaries over the past few decades, including Captivated: The Trials of Pamela Smart, and has also inspired a wide range of fiction, film, and television.

Among the most notable adaptations are the TV movie Murder in New Hampshire: The Pamela Wojas Smart Story, an episode of Law & Order, Joyce Maynard’s 1992 novel To Die For (which Gus Van Sant adapted into the 1995 dark comedy starring Nicole Kidman and Joaquin Phoenix), and Marge Piercy’s novel The Longings of Women.

items.headline: Commission preliminarily finds Temu in breach of the DSA over illegal products (17 November)
items.summary: it says Temu failed to put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective measures against the risk of illegal products, citing ineffective product-compliance controls, weak content moderation and an ineffective sanction system.
items.matters: findings are preliminary, so Temu can respond before any final decision. Marketplaces should treat product-compliance checks, moderation and seller sanctions as the areas under scrutiny.
items.body:
The European Commission preliminarily found Temu in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) obligation to put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective measures to mitigate the risk of illegal products being offered on its platform.

The Commission preliminarily found that Temu's mitigation measures include ineffective controls to check the compliance of products; a weak content moderation system; and an ineffective sanction system.

Shopping online should not mean risking the purchase of illegal and unsafe products. Under the Digital Services Act, platforms are responsible for protecting users from the risk of illegal content and goods. The preliminary findings against Temu mark another step towards making the online world safer.

items.headline: Commission preliminarily finds TikTok's "For You" feed in breach of the DSA (6 November)
items.summary: it says the recommender system can trap users in a "rabbit hole" of similar content on mental health struggles and body image, because more engagement leads to more of the same.
items.matters: the findings centre on TikTok's risk assessment and mitigation measures, so anyone shipping an engagement-driven recommender in the EU should document its systemic-risk analysis and what it does for minors.
items.body:
The European Commission has preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for the so-called ‘rabbit hole effect’ of its recommender system.

TikTok's ‘For You' feed shows users a continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image.

The more a user interacts with a certain type of content, the more TikTok's ‘For You' feed algorithm recommends similar content. This design can be harmful when such endless and repeated exposure involves, for example, content about sadness, isolation or body image. These ‘rabbit holes' can have a detrimental impact on users' mental health, especially that of vulnerable adults and minors.

items.headline: Commission study says age assurance can be proportionate and affordable (4 November)
items.summary: it finds a rights-respecting framework is workable with GDPR-consistent rules and strong privacy standards, and says costs should stay modest for most services and fall over time. It backs the EU age-verification blueprint as one of the cheapest options for providers of all sizes.
items.matters: it was commissioned to inform the proposed EU KIDS Act, so teams building apps that children use should expect age-assurance requirements and watch the blueprint.
items.body:
An independent study analyses the impacts of age assurance on fundamental rights and the costs for businesses concerned.

Age assurance is key for a safer online environment as it ensures that children only access online services and features that are safe and age appropriate for them. Nowadays, 1 in 3 children, aged 9 to 11 across 6 European countries, reports having a social media profile. Very few services are implementing age assurance in a systematic way.

To further strengthen the preparation of the proposed EU KIDS Act and the accompanying Staff Working Document, the European Commission procured a study to:

items.headline: Noema on China's gene-editing deaths
items.summary: Jane Qiu's essay (18 November, about 3,000–3,500 words) uses the death of a four-year-old in a Shanghai gene-therapy trial to ask what it reveals about China's investigator-initiated trial system. She argues that weak hospital oversight, institutional incentives and limited regulatory expertise let risky experiments proceed, and that new rules alone won't fix it.
